keywords.def: used to emphasise how much someone loves or enjoys something
a particular experience, activity, or feeling that someone finds very enjoyable and satisfying
person who has changed their beliefs or way of living
small bit of food you eat between meals, like crisps or a chocolate bar

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC英语教学的“6分钟英语”。

sentences.en: I'm Georgie. And I'm Beth. Georgie, what do apples, carrots and celery have in common with insects like beetles, crickets and grasshoppers?
sentences.zh: 我是乔治。我是贝丝。乔治，苹果、胡萝卜和西红柿有什么共同点，跟甲虫、蟋蟀和蚂蚱这些昆虫一样？

sentences.en: Hmm, that's a tough one, Beth. I'm going to say I can fit them all in my backpack.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这挺难回答的，贝丝。我猜它们都能塞进我的双肩包里。

sentences.en: OK. Well, the answer is actually, they're all examples of foods that crunch.
sentences.zh: 好的。其实答案是，它们都是会发出嘎吱声的食物的例子。

sentences.en: There's something very satisfying about the crunch when you bite into a fresh apple, a stick of celery, or even a roasted beetle!
sentences.zh: 当你咬下一口新鲜的苹果、一根西红柿，甚至是一只烤甲虫时，那种嘎吱作响的声音会带来非常满足的感觉！

sentences.en: Yes, that's right. In some parts of the world, edible insects are crunched too.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。在世界某些地方，可食用的昆虫也是嘎吱嘎吱吃的。

sentences.en: Scientist Danielle Reed has been exploring our love of crunchy food for BBC World Service programme, The Food Chain.
sentences.zh: 科学家丹妮尔·里德一直在为BBC世界服务部的节目《食物链》探索我们对酥脆食物的喜爱。

sentences.en: A crunch of a fresh apple is nothing better in the world, honestly, to me.
sentences.zh: 老实说，对我和世界上任何人来说，咬一口新鲜苹果的嘎吱声是无可比拟的。

sentences.en: I grew up as a small child in an apple orchard and so we could pick them fresh off the tree.
sentences.zh: 我在一个苹果园里长大，所以我们可以直接从树上摘下来吃。

sentences.en: And so I have a very nuanced understanding of the different crunches of apples and the different types of apples.
sentences.zh: 因此，我对苹果不同的嘎吱声和不同品种的苹果有着非常细腻的理解。

sentences.en: And so, yes, I really find that to be one of life's real true pleasures.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我真的觉得这是生活中真正的乐趣之一。

sentences.en: Danielle says there's nothing better in the world than the crunch of a fresh apple.
sentences.zh: 丹妮尔说，世界上没有什么比咬一口新鲜苹果的嘎吱声更好的了。

sentences.en: She uses the phrase, nothing better in the world,to emphasise how much she loves it.
sentences.zh: 她用了“世界上没有什么比这更好的了”这个短语来强调她有多么喜爱它。

sentences.en: Danielle thinks eating crunchy apples is one of life's true pleasures – an experience she finds enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 丹妮尔认为吃酥脆的苹果是生活真正的乐趣之一——这是一段她觉得很享受的经历。

sentences.en: But why are we so attracted to crunchy food?
sentences.zh: 但是为什么我们这么喜欢酥脆的食物呢？

sentences.en: That's what we'll be investigating in this programme, along with some useful new vocabulary, all of which you can find on our website bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在本期节目中要探讨的内容，同时还有一些有用的新词汇，你都可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 但首先，乔治，我有一个问题要问你。

sentences.en: Like Danielle, many British people enjoy the crunch of an apple, but according to a 2024 YouGov study, which is the most popular type of apple in the UK?
sentences.zh: 和丹妮尔一样，很多英国人也很享受咬苹果时的嘎吱声，但根据2024年YouGov的一项研究，英国最受欢迎的苹果是哪一种？

sentences.en: Is it: a) Pink Lady, b) Gala, or c) Red Delicious?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 粉红佳人，b) 嘎啦，还是 c) 红地厘蛇？

sentences.en: I'm going to say a) Pink Lady, because that's my favourite.
sentences.zh: 我选 a) 粉红佳人，因为那是我的最爱。

sentences.en: Ah, and me! OK. We'll find out the answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 啊，我也是！好的。我们会在节目晚些时候揭晓答案。

sentences.en: As well as the satisfying sound of a loud crunch, the texture of crunchy food is important too.
sentences.zh: 除了响亮嘎吱声带来的满足感外，酥脆食物的口感也很重要。

sentences.en: It tells our bodies to get ready for the raw and rough fibre needed to develop our chewing muscles and teeth.
sentences.zh: 它告诉我们的身体准备好迎接发育咀嚼肌和牙齿所需的生硬纤维。

sentences.en: And there are other ways in which crunchy food keeps us healthy, as Danielle explains to BBC World Service's The Food Chain.
sentences.zh: 正如丹妮尔向BBC世界服务部的《食物链》节目解释的那样，酥脆食物还有其他方式让我们保持健康。

sentences.en: The first bite of crunch is the most essential bite because, really, when we put something in our mouth, we don't think about it this way, but we have to decide whether we're going to swallow, right?
sentences.zh: 第一口咬下去的嘎吱声是最关键的一口，因为实际上，当我们把东西放进嘴里时，我们不会这样想，但我们必须决定是否要吞咽，对吧？

sentences.en: So that first bite gives us a ton of information.
sentences.zh: 所以这第一口能给我们提供大量的信息。

sentences.en: I mean, everybody, I think, has had the experience of biting into a mushy apple and saying, "No thank you!"
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为每个人都有过咬一口软绵绵的苹果然后说“不用了谢谢”的经历。

sentences.en: So, the crunch is telling us about the quality of food, specifically the high quality of the food.
sentences.zh: 所以，嘎吱声是在向我们传递关于食物质量的信息，具体来说就是食物的高品质。

sentences.en: Yes. Or not – you know, we've also had cases where we've bitten into something that has a crunch and found an eggshell in our scrambled eggs.
sentences.zh: 是的。或者没有——你知道的，我们也遇到过咬到嘎吱作响的东西却在炒鸡蛋里发现蛋壳的情况。

sentences.en: That's no good! When we put food in our mouths, we need to know it's safe.
sentences.zh: 那可不好！当我们把食物放进嘴里时，我们需要知道它是安全的。

sentences.en: A loud crunch means, this food is fresh and OK to eat.
sentences.zh: 响亮的嘎吱声意味着这种食物很新鲜，可以放心食用。

sentences.en: The crunching sound gives us a ton of information, meaning a lot of information, about the food's freshness.
sentences.zh: 嘎吱声给我们提供了大量的信息，意思是关于食物新鲜度的很多信息。

sentences.en: Nobody likes biting into an apple which is mushy, an adjective meaning soft, because we understand that that means it's bad to eat.
sentences.zh: 没有人喜欢咬一个软绵绵的苹果，“软绵绵”是一个意为质地变软的形容词，因为我们知道这意味着它不能吃了。

sentences.en: So crunchy food sounds healthy, feels good, and tells our body it's safe to eat.
sentences.zh: 所以酥脆的食物听起来很健康，感觉很好，并且告诉我们的身体可以安全食用。

sentences.en: No wonder that when astronauts on the International Space Station were asked what they missed the most, crunchy food topped their list!
sentences.zh: 难怪当国际空间站的宇航员被问到他们最想念什么时，酥脆的食物排在了他们的榜首！

sentences.en: But apples and carrots are one thing, Beth – it's something else to crunch down on insects, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但苹果和胡萝卜是一回事，贝丝——咬昆虫可是另一码事，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, not in some countries, Georgie – Zimbabwe for one, where celebrity chef, Dulsie Mudekwa, uses the crunchy texture of beetles, termites, and locusts to convince people to try insect protein as a cheap alternative to meat.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在某些国家并非如此，乔治——比如津巴布韦，名人厨师杜尔西·穆德夸利用甲虫、白蚁和蝗虫的酥脆口感，说服人们尝试将昆虫蛋白质作为肉类的廉价替代品。

sentences.en: And if you think you could never eat insects, listen as Dulsie explains how she changed her mind to Ruth Alexander, presenter of BBC World Service programme, The Food Chain.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得你永远不会吃昆虫，听听杜尔西如何向BBC世界服务部《食物链》节目的主持人露丝·亚历山大解释她是如何改变想法的。

sentences.en: So, are you an insect convert then? Now I am.
sentences.zh: 那么，你现在是昆虫的皈依者了吗？我现在是的。

sentences.en: I love them as small snacks,just roasted with salt… or what I did with most of them is turn them into flours and meals, so I make them into cakes, biscuits.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢把它们当小零食，只用盐烤着吃……或者我把它们做成粉末和面粉，所以我把它们做成蛋糕、饼干。

sentences.en: I grind them together with chicken or beef and then turn them into beautiful sausages, and then that's how I love them.
sentences.zh: 我把它们和鸡肉或牛肉一起磨碎，然后做成美味的香肠，这就是我喜欢它们的方式。

sentences.en: Ruth asks Dulsie if she's an insect convert, a person who has changed their ideas or way of living, and Dulsie replies, "Yes." She didn't before, but now she loves eating roast insects as snacks, small bits of food you eat between meals.
sentences.zh: 露丝问杜尔西她是否是一个昆虫的皈依者——即改变了想法或生活方式的人，杜尔西回答说“是的”。她以前不吃，但现在她喜欢把烤昆虫当零食吃，也就是两餐之间吃的小份食物。

sentences.en: Hmm, they do sound crunchy… but I think I'll stick to apples thanks, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 嗯，听起来确实很脆……但我还是吃苹果吧，谢谢你，乔治。

sentences.en: Well, speaking of apples, it's time you revealed the answer to your question.
sentences.zh: 说到苹果，是时候揭晓你问题的答案了。

sentences.en: Yes, I asked you which was the most popular apple, according to a survey of people in the UK.
sentences.zh: 是的，我问过你根据一项对英国人的调查，哪种苹果最受欢迎。

sentences.en: I said Pink Lady, didn't I? You did and... it was the correct answer.
sentences.zh: 我说是粉红佳人，对吧？你说了，而且……那是正确答案。

sentences.en: Well done! Yay! OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with two positive phrases – nothing better in the world, which is used to emphasise how much someone enjoys something, and one of life's true pleasures, which describes a particular experience or activity that someone finds enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 干得好！太棒了！好的。让我们复习一下我们学过的词汇，从两个积极的短语开始——“世界上没有什么比这更好的了”，用来强调某人有多么享受某事；以及“生活真正的乐趣之一”，用来描述某人觉得愉快的一段特定经历或活动。

sentences.en: A ton of something means a lot of something.
sentences.zh: “一吨某物”意思是很多某物。

sentences.en: If you describe food as mushy, you mean it's soft – the opposite of crunchy.
sentences.zh: 如果你把食物描述为软绵绵的，你是说它很软——与酥脆相反。

sentences.en: A convert is a person who has changed their beliefs or way of living.
sentences.zh: 皈依者是指改变了信仰或生活方式的人。

sentences.en: And finally, a snack is a small bit of food you eat between meals – for example, crisps or a chocolate bar.
sentences.zh: 最后，零食是你在两餐之间吃的一小块食物——例如薯片或巧克力棒。

sentences.en: And once again our six minutes are up, but if you're ready for more, just head over to our website bbclearningenglish.com for a quiz and worksheet for this programme.
sentences.zh: 我们的6分钟时间又到了，但如果你还想学更多，只需访问我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com，获取本期节目的小测验和练习单。

sentences.en: See you there soon. Bye! Bye!
sentences.zh: 很快再见。再见！再见！
